_note: aniq_baseline_independent_cnn (required baseline 1, independent CNNs): two separate ResNet-50s fine-tuned on DPD-Small train, one predicting the crop (55 classes), one the disease (175 classes). Each network only ever sees its own label. For the shared 333-pair evaluation their outputs are combined as log P(crop) + log P(disease), so unseen pairs can be predicted from a seen crop plus a seen disease. Same validation procedure and gamma calibration as the CLIP versions, so the comparison is fair. Both networks are scored at the same epoch when choosing the epoch count.
_result: Strong baseline: beats every CLIP version. With gamma 6.5 (log-prob units, from 3 validation splits, epoch 18): harmonic mean 59.7% top-1 / 87.7% top-5, vs the best proposed model v4.1 at 52.9% / 87.1%. Seen top-1 54.9% (v4.1 44.3%), unseen top-1 65.5% (v4.1 65.7%). So the CNN's advantage is on the SEEN pairs (fine-tuned image features: crop correct 90%, disease 69% uncalibrated), while unseen accuracy is level with CLIP, and the unseen-only diagnostic (75.8%) equals v4.2 (75.6%). Uncalibrated it is the classic seen-biased baseline: unseen top-1 8.2%, HM 14.5%, only 0.2% of seen images predicted as unseen; calibration is what makes it competitive. Validation mean HM 50.9% (per split [0.4527, 0.5089, 0.5647]). Calibration still overshoots slightly (27.7% of seen-test images go to unseen pairs). Per unseen pair: sugarcane_rust 97%, mango_anthracnose 95%, cucumber_downy_mildew 94%, cucumber_powdery_mildew 81%, tomato_early_blight 74%, pepper_bell_bacterial_spot 72%, corn_brown_spot 46%, grape_black_rot 42%, cotton_bacterial_blight 38%, cherry_aphis_spp 35%. Implication for the proposed model: a frozen CLIP image encoder limits seen-pair discrimination; fine-tuning (part of) the image encoder is the obvious next step.

data._note: Same splits and 333-pair protocol as the CLIP versions (generalised zero-shot).

model._note: ResNet-50 with ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V2): a standard, well-understood CNN for the required baseline, small enough to fine-tune fully on the 6 GB GPU. One linear head per target with dropout 0.3.

input._note: Images are pre-resized once to shorter side 256 (runs/cache/resized_256) so training is not bottlenecked on decoding 3120 px JPEGs. Train: random resized crop 224. Test: resize 256, centre crop 224. ImageNet mean/std.

augmentation._note: Standard field-robustness augmentation: random resized crop (scale 0.25-1), horizontal and vertical flips (leaf orientation is arbitrary), brightness/contrast/saturation jitter 0.2. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic (yellow halos, orange rust, purple tints), see the symptom research.

loss._note: Cross-entropy with label smoothing 0.1 (long-tailed, noisy labels: median 7 images per pair). For the multi-task model the two head losses are summed with equal weight.

optimizer._note: AdamW; backbone 1e-4 (pretrained, small steps), heads 1e-3 (random init), weight decay 0.05. Cosine decay per step over the run.

validation._note: Same validation split procedure and settings as v4.2 (pseudo-unseen pairs held out, healthy excluded, 40 images per held-out pair, real unseen pairs hidden), so gamma is chosen the same way for baselines and the proposed model. gamma_grid is in log-probability units here (pair score = sum of two log-probs), so its range differs from the CLIP versions' cosine units: 0 to 10, step 0.1.

training._note: Batch 32, AMP (channels-last was 4.5x slower on this GPU, see train_cnn.py). max_epochs bounds stage 1; stage 2 refits on all training images for the selected epoch count.

evaluation._note: Pair score = log P(crop) + log P(disease). gamma (subtracted from seen pairs) from validation, in log-probability units.

runtime._note: 4 dataloader workers; images come from the resized cache.
